title: Functions Calling Functions
goal: In this lesson you will learn how one function can call another so you can build bigger behavior from small pieces.
learn: Call one function from inside another
Use a returned value from the inner call
Keep each function focused on one job
idea: One function can call another. That is normal and useful. Example: grade picks a letter. print_report calls grade, then prints a full line. Each function does one clear job. Together they make a small report.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change Ava's score from 95 to 88. Press Run. Ava's line should now show Grade: B.

practice.text: Finish grade(score) and print_report(name, score). The report function should call grade and print one line.
practice.hint: print_report already calls grade and saves the letter. Fill in print() with name, score, and letter in one message.
practice.starterTip: Try print(name, "scored", score, "- Grade:", letter) inside print_report. Like the lesson example.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if grade returns a letter, print_report calls grade, and a report line is printed using name and score.

practice.text: Finish double(n) so it returns n * 2, and show(n) so it prints the doubled value by calling double. Call show once.
practice.hint: show already uses double(n). Finish double's return, then add one line at the bottom that calls show with a number.
practice.starterTip: Use return n * 2 in double, then add show(6) (or any number) on a blank line at the end.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if double returns n*2, show calls double and prints, and show is called at least once.

quiz.question: Can one function call another function?

options.text: No, that always causes an error
Yes. That is a normal way to build programs
Only if both functions are named main

quiz.correct: Functions can call other functions to build bigger behavior from small pieces.
quiz.wrong: Yes, one function can call another. That is common and useful.

quiz.question: In the lesson code, who decides the letter grade: print_report or grade?

options.text: grade returns the letter; print_report uses it
Neither. Python picks a random grade

quiz.correct: grade does one job (pick the letter). print_report does one job (show the report).
quiz.wrong: grade returns the letter. print_report calls grade and prints the line.

quiz.question: Why call a helper function instead of copying its code?

options.text: So each job lives in one place you can reuse
Python requires at least ten functions

quiz.correct: One helper, many callers. Easier to fix and reuse.
quiz.wrong: Reuse and clear jobs are the point of calling helpers.

project.title: Points Board
project.desc: Write points(wins) that returns wins * 3. Write show_team(name, wins) that calls points and prints the team line. Call show_team for two teams.
